chatgpt.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt.notes: Business/API data is covered by separate Business Terms + DPA (openai.com/policies hub lists them) but no single canonical DPA URL surfaced in search; not fabricating one.

claude.name: Claude
claude.notes: Consumer terms confirmed via direct fetch. Commercial Terms/DPA differ from consumer; used the consumer-facing set since ChatGPT-equivalent product here is the consumer app. privacy_policy originally pointed at the privacy.claude.com portal root, which is a nav/index page with no real prose (639 chars of menu text, confirmed empty extraction even after the HTML-cleaning fix) -- swapped to the direct 'Is my data used for model training?' article, which answers the exact fact the pipeline extracts.

gemini.name: Gemini
gemini.notes: Gemini Apps Privacy Notice supplements the general Google Privacy Policy rather than standing alone; used the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub as the most specific public page.

microsoft-copilot.name: Microsoft Copilot
microsoft-copilot.notes: Consumer Copilot (for individuals) product line, distinct from Microsoft 365 Copilot enterprise product which has its own terms.

github-copilot.name: GitHub Copilot
github-copilot.notes: Free/Pro/Pro+ vs Business/Enterprise have different data-use terms (Business/Enterprise excluded from AI-training data use per GitHub's own changelog) — worth surfacing to admin reviewer since one product covers two different data postures.

windsurf.name: Windsurf
windsurf.notes: Rebranded from Codeium; search only turned up a combined terms-of-service page (privacy content embedded in it), no standalone privacy-policy URL — not fabricating one. CORRECTION (2026-08-17): earlier note said 'acquired by OpenAI' — wrong. Confirmed live: windsurf.com/terms-of-service-individual now 308-redirects permanently to devin.ai/windsurf/terms-of-service-individual, i.e. Windsurf was acquired by Cognition (maker of Devin), not OpenAI. See DECISIONS_NEEDED.md for why this domain still can't be fetched. UPDATE (third batch, 2026-08-18): confirmed directly this time via Cognition's own privacy policy — Cognition's single privacy policy explicitly covers 'Devin and Windsurf' together. See the new 'devin' entry below for the disjoint-domain detail (devin.ai / windsurf.com product domains vs. cognition.com legal domain).

sourcegraph-cody.name: Sourcegraph Cody
sourcegraph-cody.notes: Confirmed still active as of June 2026 privacy policy update; Cody is now bundled under Sourcegraph's broader "AI Tools" umbrella rather than a standalone product name.

adobe-firefly.name: Adobe Firefly
adobe-firefly.notes: No Firefly-specific privacy policy URL exists separately — Firefly is covered by Adobe's general Privacy Policy plus a dedicated 'data and content usage' explainer page, used here as the closest thing to a security/trust page.

grammarly.name: Grammarly
grammarly.notes: Individual-account privacy policy explicitly does not cover Business/Education/Pro-under-org accounts, which fall under a separate DPA — same two-tier pattern as GitHub Copilot.

jasper.name: Jasper
jasper.notes: DPA exists but must be separately executed by customers per Jasper's own terms; no public standalone DPA URL found.

notion-ai.name: Notion AI
notion-ai.notes: Used the AI-specific security/privacy practices page as the closest thing to AI-scoped terms; general Notion ToS covers the rest of the product.

zoom-ai-companion.name: Zoom AI Companion
zoom-ai-companion.notes: Zoom's general Terms of Service page used since no AI Companion-specific ToS URL surfaced separately from the privacy/security explainer.

tabnine.name: Tabnine
tabnine.notes: Privacy policy is thin on whether code is used for training -- the concrete 'zero data retention' claim lives on a separate marketing page (tabnine.com/code-privacy) that isn't a legal document, so not substituted in as the source of record. Trust center is SafeBase-hosted (third-party), same pattern as other vendor trust portals in this batch -- confirmed genuine, not a spoof.

amazon-q-developer.name: Amazon Q Developer
amazon-q-developer.notes: SHARED APEX DOMAIN (aws.amazon.com covers all AWS services) -- flag for shared_domain like Gemini/Microsoft Copilot in the first batch; the general AWS Privacy Notice and Service Terms are not Q-Developer-specific. Used the AWS docs data-protection page as security_trust_page since it's the most product-scoped source and links onward to the real opt-out mechanism (docs.aws.amazon.com/.../opt-out-IDE.html) and the service-improvement page explaining how content may be used. Confirmed via direct fetch (not a search summary) -- got real AWS doc markdown, not a nav shell. UPDATE (2026-08-18 deep dive, see research/deep_dive_amazonq_speechify_deepl.md): the two facts previously left null resolve cleanly via dedicated AWS docs pages -- Free tier content (incl. code/prompts) may be used for service improvement/model training with a working per-IDE opt-out toggle ('Amazon Q: Share Content'); Pro tier never collects content at all. Recommend rating on Free tier per the same ICP precedent set for DeepL.

jetbrains-ai-assistant.name: JetBrains AI Assistant
jetbrains-ai-assistant.notes: AI-specific ToS states inputs/outputs will NOT be used to train language models without express permission -- a clearer no-default-training stance than most tools in this batch. DPA page is dated Version 1.3 / April 27, 2022 -- old relative to the 2025-dated AI ToS it's linked from; flagging staleness, not swapping it for a guess.

bolt-new.name: Bolt.new
bolt-new.notes: Bolt.new has no standalone legal docs -- StackBlitz (the parent company/IDE product) is the entity and its Privacy Policy/ToS explicitly cover Bolt. Confirmed the privacy policy addresses AI-input training use directly (tiered opt-out by plan). A separate merch-shop ToS at shop.bolt.new/pages/terms-of-service exists but is irrelevant (covers t-shirt purchases, not the product) -- not used.

v0.name: v0
v0.notes: SHARED APEX DOMAIN for the privacy/terms/DPA docs (vercel.com covers Vercel's whole hosting platform, not just v0) -- same flag as Amazon Q Developer. Used v0.app/policy (confirmed genuine, product-specific) as the security_trust_page slot since it's the one v0-scoped legal doc and covers the actual fact this pipeline extracts: tiered model-training opt-in/opt-out by plan tier.

ideogram.name: Ideogram
ideogram.notes: Privacy policy confirms user data is used to 'train the models that power our Services' with no opt-out mechanism found, and no GDPR-specific section (policy leans CCPA/state-law framing). Worth a clear-eyed read before publishing as compliant on anything.

luma-ai.name: Luma AI (Dream Machine)
luma-ai.notes: Confirms data used to 'train, develop, and improve' its AI/ML models; no explicit training opt-out found (only marketing-email opt-out), despite an otherwise thorough GDPR rights section. Enterprise customers are carved out as controllers under their own terms.

suno.name: Suno
suno.notes: ToS grants Suno a broad perpetual license over submissions/outputs 'in connection with...improvement of our products and services, including...artificial intelligence and machine learning models' -- confirmed via direct fetch. Free vs. paid tiers have different output-ownership terms, similar two-tier pattern to GitHub Copilot/Grammarly in the first batch.

heygen.name: HeyGen
heygen.notes: One of the few tools in this batch with an explicit AI-training opt-out reachable by contacting privacy@heygen.com (Section 4 of the privacy policy) rather than just a settings toggle. security.heygen.com is a Drata-hosted trust portal (third-party-hosted, same pattern as Tabnine's SafeBase portal) -- confirmed genuine, not mistaken for an unrelated org's trust center.

synthesia.name: Synthesia
synthesia.notes: Used the consumer-facing User Terms of Service (not Customer Terms of Service, which is the B2B contract) to match this batch's individual-checker ICP, same distinction made for ChatGPT/GitHub Copilot in the first batch. Privacy policy does not clearly state whether personal data (as opposed to video/avatar content generally) is used for model training -- flagging the gap rather than guessing.

wordtune.name: Wordtune
wordtune.notes: Privacy policy says content is used to 'improve, enhance and develop the Services' but doesn't clearly say whether that includes AI model training specifically -- ambiguous rather than silent. Confirmed strong GDPR section otherwise.

sudowrite.name: Sudowrite
sudowrite.notes: FLAG FOR REVIEWER: privacy policy is dated October 6, 2020 and never mentions AI, model training, or generative features at all, despite Sudowrite being an AI fiction-writing tool today -- reads as a stale template the company hasn't updated to cover its actual product. Confirmed genuine (not fabricated), just outdated; extraction will likely come back with null training-related facts, which is an honest reflection of the source, not a pipeline bug.

you-com.name: You.com
you-com.notes: Privacy policy explicitly states uploaded/prompt data 'will not be used for developing, improving, or training third party AI and/or ML models' -- one of the clearer no-third-party-training statements in this batch (says nothing about You.com's own first-party models, worth noting).

kagi.name: Kagi
kagi.notes: No separate terms-of-service URL surfaced distinct from the privacy policy -- Kagi's site structures both under /privacy plus a linked 'Privacy Rights Addendum' for GDPR/CCPA specifics; used the same URL for both fields rather than fabricate a separate ToS link. Policy states Kagi does not use personal data or prompts to train AI models and does not sell data -- a genuinely privacy-first stance consistent with its no-ads subscription business model.

fireflies-ai.name: Fireflies.ai
fireflies-ai.notes: Explicit statement that meeting content/personal data is not used to train AI models and vendors are contractually barred from training on it -- one of the strongest no-training claims found in this batch.

rev.name: Rev
rev.notes: Policy doesn't explicitly address AI-model-training use of transcripts/audio, a notable gap for a company whose product is AI-assisted transcription -- flagging rather than inferring an answer from marketing copy that says 'never uses customer content to train external AI models' (that claim wasn't confirmed inside the legal document itself).

speechify.name: Speechify
speechify.notes: Speechify also runs separate Studio-specific privacy/terms pages (speechify.com/studio-privacy, speechify.com/studio-terms) for its voice-cloning/dubbing product line -- used the main consumer text-to-speech app's policy since that's the product a casual checker would have installed, not the Studio B2B tool. UPDATE (2026-08-18 deep dive, see research/deep_dive_amazonq_speechify_deepl.md): trains_on_user_data and opt_out_available should stay null -- genuinely unresolved. The operative clause ('improve the features, algorithms...of our Services' / ToS Section 7 'internal business purposes...commercially benefit') is broad enough to cover AI training but never uses the words 'train,' 'AI,' 'machine learning,' or 'model' -- unlike the Google Workspace carve-out, which explicitly says AI/ML training does NOT happen for that one data source, leaving ordinary app data unstated rather than confirmed either way. No opt-out mechanism for AI training found anywhere. Also flagged: speechify.ai (a distinct 'SpeechifyAI' enterprise/API entity, copyright '© 2026 SpeechifyAI') and speechify-app.com both surfaced in search claiming Speechify-adjacent privacy claims -- neither used as a source of record, relationship to Speechify Inc. unconfirmed.

character-ai.name: Character.AI
character-ai.notes: FLAG FOR REVIEWER: both URLs are confirmed genuine and resolve on the real character.ai domain (via 308 redirects from policies.character.ai, which is the canonical link Character.AI itself publishes) -- but the site is a client-rendered SPA, so WebFetch only received the page shell/tagline, not policy prose, on every attempt. This is the same failure mode as Claude's nav-page issue in the first batch, except here it's a rendering limitation, not a wrong URL -- the backend's own fetcher may hit the same wall depending on whether it executes JS. Also checked and explicitly rejected a lookalike domain, characterai.cc, which appeared in search results claiming to host Character.AI's terms -- it is not Character.AI's domain and was not used anywhere in this record.

poe.name: Poe
poe.notes: Poe's privacy policy is a supplement to the main Quora Privacy Policy (incorporated by reference) rather than fully standalone -- confirmed it explicitly discloses that third-party AI model providers and bot creators can receive full chat contents/uploaded files. No clear opt-out mechanism for that sharing found within the Poe-specific document itself.

granola.name: Granola
granola.notes: Confirms Granola does not allow OpenAI/Anthropic/other third-party model providers to train on customer data, only uses de-identified/aggregated data for its own model improvement, and that's opt-outable in account settings (opt-out is default-off for Enterprise). Newer, smaller consumer-facing tool -- exactly the category the founder asked this batch to cover.

deepl.name: DeepL
deepl.notes: Clean two-tier compliance story confirmed directly in both the privacy policy and this free-service ToS: free-tier submissions ARE used to train/improve DeepL's models (temporary retention), Pro/paid submissions explicitly are NOT. This is a genuinely different compliance answer depending on which tier a user is on -- worth surfacing to the reviewer the same way the free-vs-paid GitHub Copilot split was flagged in the first batch. Used the free-service Terms of Use (matches this batch's individual/casual ICP) rather than the Pro/Enterprise license variants, which are separate documents. UPDATE (2026-08-18 deep dive, see research/deep_dive_amazonq_speechify_deepl.md): per Elliot's 2026-08-18 confirmation, rate on the free tier for ICP-consistency -- trains_on_user_data: true, opt_out_available: false (no opt-out mechanism exists for free-tier users; switching to Pro is a tier change, not an opt-out setting). Pro tier's 'not used to improve our services' statement (Privacy Policy Section 4) independently corroborated by the Pro License Agreement -- keep as caveat text on the badge, not the rated value.

devin.name: Devin
devin.notes: DISJOINT DOMAIN, flagging per the founder's Bolt.new/StackBlitz precedent rather than resolving it myself: the product lives at devin.ai, but the governing Privacy Policy/ToS/DPA all live on cognition.ai / cognition.com (cognition.ai/privacy-policy 301-redirects to cognition.com/privacy-policy -- confirmed via direct fetch, used the redirected URL as source of record). It's a three-way version of the pattern too: Cognition's single privacy policy explicitly covers both 'Devin and Windsurf' by name (Cognition acquired Windsurf -- see the updated windsurf entry above), so one legal document spans two differently-branded, differently-domained consumer products (devin.ai and windsurf.com). Training-use language: 'using User Content to train, fine tune and improve the models that power our Services' under 'Legitimate Interests,' but the policy adds this 'depends on the terms that apply to your use of the Services' -- implies a plan/tier split similar to GitHub Copilot's, without spelling out the tiers in the privacy policy itself. No self-serve opt-out found in the privacy policy; contact is privacy@cognition.ai. security_trust_page is a SafeBase-hosted trust center (same third-party-hosted pattern as Tabnine/HeyGen in the second batch) -- confirmed genuine.

warp.name: Warp
warp.notes: AI terminal / agentic dev environment. Confirmed via direct fetch: policy discloses using data to train/fine-tune/improve AI-feature models, but the specific language is vague on whether that covers terminal/code content vs. just AI prompts. Separately, terminal-session content storage and AI prompt/output collection are each independently opt-out-able in Settings ('Active AI'/'Agent Mode' prompts, and general terminal-data sharing). Zero Data Retention is Enterprise-plan-only, not available on the free/individual tier -- worth a reviewer's eye, similar tier-gated-privacy-feature pattern as other tools in this batch, though not a full training-use tier split like DeepL's.

zed.name: Zed
zed.notes: AI code editor. Confirmed via direct fetch: code/prompts sent through Zed's hosted AI models are discarded after each request and never used for training, backed by Zero Data Retention agreements with Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and xAI (one named exception: certain Anthropic 'Covered Models' require short-term provider-side retention for safety). Explicitly opt-in (not opt-out) by design for any data sharing, e.g. Edit Prediction training-data sharing is off by default and, when turned on, limited to open-source code under permissive licenses. One of the stronger privacy postures found across all three batches so far.

continue-dev.name: Continue.dev
continue-dev.notes: Open-source-first coding assistant (works with local/self-hosted models). Confirmed via direct fetch: privacy notice (last updated Feb 5, 2026) does not discuss AI training use of code/prompts one way or the other -- a real gap, not inferred. FLAG FOR REVIEWER: a WebSearch result title read 'Continue (acquired by Cursor)' (via Y Combinator's company page), suggesting a recent acquisition by Anysphere/Cursor (already a separate catalog entry) -- not confirmed inside Continue's own privacy policy or terms, and not independently verified beyond that one search-result label. If confirmed, this would eventually make Continue.dev and Cursor commonly-owned products on separate domains, similar in shape to the Devin/Windsurf/Cognition situation above -- flagging now rather than waiting for it to surface as a surprise later.

perplexity-comet.name: Perplexity Comet
perplexity-comet.notes: AI browser, same vendor as the already-catalogued 'Perplexity AI' entry but a materially different product with its own dedicated privacy notice (not just the main Perplexity Privacy Notice) covering local/on-device browsing data specifically. FLAG: same apex domain (perplexity.ai) as the existing Perplexity AI catalog entry -- expect the shared_domain heuristic to fire even though, unlike the AWS/Vercel cases, this is genuinely the same company/product family rather than unrelated products sharing infrastructure; still worth a reviewer's eye on how the heuristic should treat same-vendor multi-product cases differently from true shared-apex-domain cases. FLAG: direct WebFetch verification failed with HTTP 403 on two separate attempts; the specific facts above (on-device-by-default storage, opt-in/opt-out for site/service integrations, 30-day auto-deletion of queries Comet classifies as personal) are sourced from WebSearch's summary of the live page, not independently confirmed via a raw fetch -- treat as secondary-sourced pending a successful direct fetch.

fathom.name: Fathom
fathom.notes: AI meeting notetaker. Confirmed via direct fetch. Fathom uses de-identified meeting-content data to train/improve its own in-house AI models, with a self-serve opt-out in account settings; explicitly does NOT authorize third-party model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.) to train on personal information or meeting content. Note for future sourcing passes: several similarly-named domains exist (fathomhq.com, fathomthat.ai, fathom.video) -- fathom.ai was the one confirmed via direct fetch to be Fathom Video Inc.'s real domain; the others were not checked in enough depth to rule in or out, not used as sources here.

krisp.name: Krisp
krisp.notes: AI meeting assistant / noise-cancellation. Confirmed via direct fetch: third-party app/service data (e.g. Google Workspace) explicitly excluded from generalized AI/ML training. For Krisp's own proprietary models, the policy lists 'Improving our proprietary AI models and providing more accurate services' as a consent-based purpose -- i.e. framed as requiring affirmative consent rather than default-on-with-opt-out, but no dedicated settings-level opt-out toggle was found distinct from that initial consent choice. Noise-cancellation-only usage keeps audio entirely on-device (never reaches Krisp's servers); the training/data-sharing questions above apply to the transcription/meeting-assistant features specifically.

tldv.name: tl;dv
tldv.notes: AI meeting recorder/notetaker. Confirmed via direct fetch, Section 9: 'Customer Content is processed solely to provide the requested functionality and is not used by tldx Solutions GmbH or such providers to train or improve their general-purpose AI models' -- one of the clearest categorical no-training statements found across all three batches. No opt-out mechanism is specified, but the policy frames this as unnecessary since the practice doesn't happen in the first place rather than as a gap. Germany-based data controller.

donotpay.name: DoNotPay
donotpay.notes: AI legal-assistant / consumer-rights automation tool. Confirmed via direct fetch. Privacy policy is dated August 22, 2023 and does not address AI model training, machine learning, or any AI-specific data use anywhere in the document -- a real gap, not an extraction miss, for a product whose entire premise is AI-generated legal correspondence and negotiation. Worth noting for reviewer context (not a compliance fact, just background): DoNotPay has prior FTC enforcement history over AI-related marketing claims, which a search result surfaced but which is not itself part of the privacy policy.

gamma.name: Gamma
gamma.notes: AI presentation/document generator. TIER SPLIT, same pattern as DeepL/GitHub Copilot: on plans without privacy controls enabled (i.e. default/Free), Gamma may use content to train/improve/refine its models; Team and Business plans do not train on content and Business/Enterprise specifically guarantee zero data retention for training. FLAG: direct WebFetch verification failed with HTTP 403 on two separate attempts (both gamma.app/privacy); the tier-split language above is sourced from WebSearch's summary of the live page, not independently confirmed via raw fetch -- treat as secondary-sourced pending a successful direct fetch, same caveat as Perplexity Comet above.

recraft.name: Recraft
recraft.vendor: Recraft (entity name not independently confirmed beyond 'Recraft')
recraft.notes: Newer AI image-generation model. Confirmed via direct fetch: third-party AI providers are contractually barred from training on user prompts/outputs without affirmative authorization; Recraft's own proprietary models may train on that data by default, but with a self-serve opt-out in account profile settings. Separately (content-ownership axis, not a training-tier split): on the Free plan, generated/uploaded images are public and owned by Recraft (may appear in the community gallery); on paid plans, assets are private and user-owned -- worth a reviewer's eye as a different flavor of tier-dependent privacy posture than DeepL's, since it's about content visibility/ownership rather than model training. Checked and did not use a lookalike domain, recraftv3.org, that surfaced in search results.

black-forest-labs.name: Black Forest Labs (FLUX)
black-forest-labs.notes: Newer AI image-generation model (FLUX). Confirmed via direct fetch: inputs and outputs are used by default 'to train and improve our AI models' and content-moderation tooling. Opt-out exists but is manual/friction-y rather than a settings toggle -- users must email legal@blackforestlabs.ai with subject line 'Training Opt Out' and account details, similar manual-opt-out pattern to Fireflies.ai/HeyGen in the second batch rather than the cleaner self-serve toggles seen elsewhere in this batch (Fathom, Recraft).

pika.name: Pika
pika.notes: Newer AI video-generation model/app (text-to-video, 'AI Selves' digital-representation feature). FLAG FOR REVIEWER: URLs confirmed genuine (pika.art is the real product domain per multiple independent search results, and launch.pika.art / dev.pika.art are Pika's own subdomains, not lookalikes) but the privacy policy page is a client-rendered SPA -- WebFetch received only an accordion table-of-contents and page footer, never the expanded clause text, across two separate attempts (pika.art/privacy-policy and launch.pika.art/privacy-policy). Same failure mode as Character.AI in the second batch. Could not confirm or deny AI-training-use language or an opt-out mechanism as a result -- both facts should extract as null if the backend's fetcher hits the same JS wall, and that would be an honest reflection of an extraction gap, not a thin source. Also checked and explicitly rejected a lookalike domain, pika-art.net ('Pika AI: Free AI Video Generator'), which is not Mellis, Inc.'s site -- not used anywhere in this record.

kling-ai.name: Kling AI
kling-ai.notes: Newer AI video-generation model, backed by Kuaishou (China-based parent). FLAG FOR REVIEWER, low-confidence sourcing: both URLs are the ones Kling AI's own docs site publishes and match the entity name 'Kling AI Pte. Ltd' seen in search results, but direct WebFetch returned HTTP 446 (an unusual, non-standard status code -- possibly a geo-block or bot-block) on every attempt to both the privacy policy and terms pages, so nothing here was independently confirmed via raw fetch, only via WebSearch's summary of the live pages. That summary describes broad ToS license language ('worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free, and sublicensable license... often allows use of videos to train future AI models') and a paid-tier-only 'Private Mode' that hides generations from the public community gallery. Given the China-based parent company, international data-transfer/GDPR-adequacy questions are also worth a reviewer's attention beyond what this pass could confirm. Do not treat this entry's facts as verified to the same standard as the rest of this batch -- flag for a follow-up direct-fetch attempt or a different access path before it goes through extraction.

teal.name: Teal
teal.vendor: Teal (TealHQ) -- exact legal entity name not independently confirmed
teal.notes: AI resume-builder / job-search companion -- sourced to cover the HR/recruiting-adjacent gap from the individual job-seeker's side, since actual HR/recruiting-AI vendors (Workday AI, Greenhouse AI, etc.) are enterprise-only B2B infrastructure out of scope for this catalog's ICP. FLAG: direct WebFetch verification failed with HTTP 403 on two separate attempts; the summary above (resume/career content collected, no sale of personal information, user-controlled export/delete) is sourced from WebSearch's summary only. Notably, that summary surfaced no explicit statement either way on whether resume/career content is used to train Teal's AI features -- a real gap worth flagging for a reviewer even accounting for the lower-confidence sourcing here, since it's the exact fact this pipeline needs and no page text was found addressing it.

elicit.name: Elicit
elicit.notes: AI research-paper assistant. Confirmed via direct fetch on the privacy policy and DPA. FLAG FOR REVIEWER: the privacy policy (dated September 12, 2023) never discusses whether uploaded documents/research queries are used to train AI models, in either direction -- a notable silence for a product whose whole premise is AI analysis of user-supplied papers, and stale relative to the DPA it sits alongside (dated April 1, 2025), similar staleness pattern to JetBrains AI Assistant in the second batch. security_trust_page (trust.elicit.com) is referenced inside Elicit's own DPA text but was not independently fetched to confirm its contents in this pass.

superhuman.name: Superhuman
superhuman.notes: AI email client -- new category for the catalog (AI email assistant). Confirmed via direct fetch: explicit statement that Superhuman uses collected information to train its AI models, paired with a genuine self-serve opt-out via account-settings 'training control(s)' -- one of the cleanest opt-out mechanisms found across all three batches. If used under an organization's management, an org's own contract/DPA governs instead of this consumer privacy policy (same org-vs-individual carve-out pattern as several other tools in this catalog). Search also surfaced joinsuperhuman.io as a possibly-related domain; not confirmed as affiliated and not used as a source here.
